texts.li: The days are lengthening at last. {A_nameDef} wants everyone up before dawn tomorrow on the highest ground near the walls, with a fire going, to watch the sun come back after the long dark.

A notched stick, one notch for every day's light, kept by {A_nameDef} all winter. By its count the sun clears the far ridge tomorrow for the first time since the dark, and {A_nameDef} wants everyone out to see it, with a fire to stand round.

[lowtech] In {A_nameDef}'s village the first spring sunrise was met with a fire on the hill and every voice in the place shouting it up. {A_nameDef} has already started carrying wood up to the high ground.
[devout] {A_nameDef} wants the colony to greet the returning sun with a fire and the faith's morning words, the way the faithful of the cold lands always have.

li.label: Everyone up to greet the sun
li.outcome: The colony stood round a fire on the high ground in the blue before dawn, stamping their feet, until the sun cleared the ridge. They stood in it a while, faces turned up, before anyone thought of breakfast.

outcomes.li: [snow] It was snowing when they climbed up and clear when the sun came. {A_nameDef} took it as a promise.

li.label: Whoever's awake can watch it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and a handful of early risers watched the sun come up from the wall. The rest saw it through the window, and that was something.

li.label: The sun comes back without our help
li.outcome: The sun came up the way it always does, over a colony already at work. {A_nameDef} watched it alone from the woodpile.

texts.li: It's raining, really raining, for the first time in weeks. {A_nameDef} is standing in the middle of the yard with {A_possessive} face turned up, and asks if everyone could put down their tools and come out into it.

Rain at last, dark spots spreading on the dust. {A_nameDef} has already put every pot and bucket the colony owns out under the eaves, and wants the colony out in it together to welcome it, as desert people do.
[tribal] Rain has to be danced in, or it won't come back. Every child among {A_nameDef}'s people knows that, and {A_nameDef} is already barefoot in the yard.
[devout] {A_nameDef} says the rain is a gift, and gifts are given thanks for, out loud and together.

li.label: Everyone out in the rain
li.outcome: The colony stood out in the rain until they were soaked through, laughing, catching it in their hands. {A_nameDef} started a dance with no particular steps, which made it easy to join.

outcomes.li: [tribal] {A_nameDef} led the rain dance round the yard, and one by one the colony joined in, splashing, until the rain eased off as if it had been satisfied.

li.label: Catch it in every pot, then back to work
li.outcome: Every pot, bucket and trough in the colony went out under the eaves, and work went on to the sound of it drumming.

li.label: It's only rain
li.outcome: Work went on indoors. {A_nameDef} stood in the doorway a long time, watching it fall.

texts.li: The ice is off the water and the spring flood has gone down. {A_nameDef} wants the colony to walk down to the water together in the morning, say a few words over it and give it a loaf, for the fish and the crossings and the drinking water of the year.
{A_nameDef} has baked a small round loaf with a mark on top and asks the council for one morning: everyone at the water's edge, the loaf given to the water, and a word for a kind year from it.
[lowtech] No boat went out in {A_nameDef}'s village until the water had been blessed and given its bread. {A_nameDef} has the loaf baked already.
[devout] {A_nameDef} wants the faith's blessing said over the water at the start of the year, with everyone there to hear it.

li.label: Everyone to the water's edge
li.outcome: The colony stood at the water's edge in the cold morning while {A_nameDef} said the words and set the loaf on the water. It floated a long way before it went under, which everyone agreed was a good sign.

li.label: {A_nameDef} can bless it alone
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went down alone at dawn and gave the water its loaf, and came back with wet sleeves and a quiet face.

li.label: Bread is for eating
li.outcome: The loaf went on the supper table. {A_nameDef} ate a piece of it, but not as if it tasted of much.

texts.li: The fever season is here, the air thick with insects every evening. {A_nameDef} wants the colony to walk the bounds after dark with torches of green wood, the smoke driving the biting things back into the wet dark beyond the fields, and the lights telling whatever lives out there that this ground is taken.

Bundles of wet wood and reeds are stacked by {A_nameDef}'s door, a week's worth of tying. Lit, they smoke like anything. {A_nameDef} wants everyone out one evening to carry them round the colony's edge.

[lowtech] The marsh villages {A_nameDef} grew up among walk their bounds with smoking torches on the longest evening of the fever season, to keep off the biting things and the fevers with them. By {A_nameDef}'s count, that evening is tonight.

li.label: Everyone out with the torches
li.outcome: A line of smoking torches wound round the colony's edge after dark, with the colonists coughing and laughing behind them. The insects kept off for a night, and the lights could be seen a long way out into the dark.

li.label: One torch at each door
li.outcome: A smoking torch went up at every door. The insects were thinner that night, if only just.

li.label: Keep the wood for the fires
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat up late slapping at insects and muttering about green wood.

texts.li: The harvest is in and the air is clear enough to see for miles. {A_nameDef} wants the colony to climb to the high ground one evening, all of them, and look out over everything the colony has made and everything around it, before the winter closes the view.
{A_nameDef} found a ledge above the colony where you can see every field and wall at once, and the far hills beyond. {A_nameDef} says they should all see it together, once a year.
[lowtech] Hill people climb to the high stones every autumn, {A_nameDef} says, to see their land whole and count what they have. {A_nameDef} has found the right stones already.

li.label: Everyone up to the high ground
li.outcome: The colony climbed up in the late light and sat in a row on the ledge, pointing out their own roofs and fields to each other. From up there it looked like a place someone had meant to make.

li.label: Those who want to can climb
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and a few others went up at sunset and came back after dark, talking low.

li.label: We can see enough from here
li.outcome: The high ground stayed empty. {A_nameDef} kept glancing up at it all evening.

texts.li: The longest nights are here. {A_nameDef} asks that the faithful keep a vigil, as the faith has always kept one in the dark of the year: a lamp lit at dusk, the old words said through the night, and the colony gathered until the first light.

{A_nameDef} spent the afternoon trimming every lamp in the colony. Tonight, if the council allows it, they'd burn from dusk till dawn for a vigil of the faith, so the colony begins the turn of the year awake and together.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} remembers the vigils of {A_possessive} childhood: candles, the words said and answered, the cold coming in under the door. {A_nameDef} would like to keep one here.

li.label: Keep the vigil together
li.outcome: The colony gathered as the light went and kept the vigil deep into the night, the words said and answered, the lamps trimmed twice. A few fell asleep sitting up and were left to it. By first light only {A_nameDef} was still awake to say the last words.

li.label: A short vigil, then bed
li.outcome: The words were said at dusk with the lamps lit, and the colony went to bed at the usual hour. {A_nameDef}'s lamp was still burning in the morning.

li.label: Everyone needs their sleep
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} lit one lamp by {A_possessive} bed and sat up beside it, saying the words alone.

texts.li: The trees are in full leaf. {A_nameDef} asks that the colony go out to the oldest tree near the walls one afternoon and sing to it, all together, as the faith teaches: the land was here first, and it should hear that the colony knows it.

{A_nameDef} has been sitting under the big tree every evening this week, humming the same tune. Asked about it, {A_nameDef} sang the council the words: "We took your shade and we took your wood, and we thank you for both." {A_nameDef} wants them all out there once a year to sing it properly.
[tribal] "Every spring, a song for the trees." {A_nameDef}'s grandmother said it, and her people before her, so the forest would go on feeding them. {A_nameDef} would like the colony to sing too.

li.label: Everyone out to sing
li.outcome: The colony sat in a ring round the old tree all afternoon, singing the songs {A_nameDef} taught them, badly at first and then well. The leaves moved overhead the whole time, though there wasn't any wind.

li.label: A song at dusk, before supper
li.outcome: One song, at dusk, everyone standing at the edge of the trees. {A_nameDef} sang the last verse alone.

li.label: Trees don't listen
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went out alone after dark and sat a long while with {A_possessive} back to the old tree.

texts.li: The year is turning. {A_nameDef} asks for a supper with a place laid for each of the colony's dead: their bowl filled, their names said at the start, and the faith's words for those who went before. It would take about {COUNT} raw food.

{A_nameDef} has been carving little name-boards for the colony's dead, one for each, to set at a long table so they can eat with the living once a year. One evening and about {COUNT} raw food, {A_nameDef} reckons.

[lowtech] Once a year, in {A_nameDef}'s village, the dead were fed: a full bowl at the head of the table, and the door left open so they could come in. {A_nameDef} would like to lay that table here, with about {COUNT} raw food.

li.label: A place at the table for every one of them
li.outcome: The long table was laid with a place for each of the colony's dead, a full bowl at each, and {A_nameDef} said every name before anyone ate. Someone laughed at a story about one of them, and after that the stories kept coming. The door stood open the whole evening.

li.label: Say their names at supper
li.outcome: No extra places, but {A_nameDef} said every name before the meal, and people raised their cups to each.

li.label: The dead don't need feeding
li.outcome: Supper as usual. {A_nameDef} set one small bowl on the windowsill afterward, and left it there all night.
